method_card.title: Probability Basics & Tree Diagrams
method_card.content:
Probability measures how likely an event is, from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). \(P(A) = \frac{\text{favourable outcomes}}{\text{total outcomes}}\). The complement: \(P(\text{not } A) = 1 - P(A)\).

Expected frequency = probability × number of trials. Relative frequency = observed frequency ÷ number of trials.

Tree diagrams: Multiply along branches for AND, add between branches for OR. For independent events, probabilities stay the same. For without replacement, reduce the denominator on the second pick.
method_card.example:
A bag has 4 red and 6 blue balls. Find P(red).

\(P(\text{red}) = \frac{4}{4+6} = \frac{4}{10} = \frac{2}{5}\)

steps: Split the event into every path that works, e.g. red-blue AND blue-red.
Multiply along each path, then add the paths.
'At least one' is quickest as \(1 - P(\text{none})\).

steps: Count the favourable outcomes: the ones you want.
Count the total number of equally likely outcomes.
Write favourable over total, then simplify. For 'not', use \(P(\text{not }A) = 1 - P(A)\).

silver.title: Silver: two-stage probability

example.question: A bag has 3 red, 2 blue. Two picked without replacement. Find P(both red).

gold.hint: One of each happens two ways: red then blue, and blue then red. Add them.
gold.display: A bag has 6 red and 4 blue. Two picked without replacement. Find P(one of each colour) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: One of each can happen two ways: red then blue, or blue then red. Without replacement.

guided_steps.hint: Reds times blues along the path.

guided_steps.say: Blue-red is the same, 24/90. Add the two paths.

misconceptions.message: One of each happens two ways: red-blue AND blue-red, each 24/90. Add them: 48/90 = 8/15. One order alone is 24/90.

gold.hint: Three reds without replacement: reds and total both drop each pick.
gold.display: A bag has 7 red and 3 blue. Three are picked without replacement. Find P(all red) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Three reds without replacement: reds and total both drop each pick.

guided_steps.hint: One red and one ball removed.

guided_steps.say: Multiply bottoms: 10 × 9 × 8 = 720, then simplify 210/720 by 30.

misconceptions.message: The reds drop each pick: 7/10 × 6/9 × 5/8 = 7/24. Treating it as 7/10 cubed gives 343/1000.

gold.hint: Easier as 1 minus P(no heads at all).
gold.display: A coin is flipped 4 times. Find P(at least one head) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: At least one head is easiest as 1 − P(no heads at all).
So P(no heads) = 1/16, and P(at least one) = 16/16 − 1/16.

misconceptions.message: At least one head = 1 − P(no heads) = 1 − 1/16 = 15/16. 1/16 is the chance of NO heads.

gold.hint: Add the two routes to B: through A and through not A.
gold.display: P(A) = 0.6, P(B given A) = 0.5, P(B given not A) = 0.25. Find P(B) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: B can be reached two ways: through A, or through not A. Total-probability rule.

guided_steps.hint: P(not A) times P(B given not A).

guided_steps.say: Add the paths: 0.30 + 0.10 = 0.4 = 4/10. Simplify by 2.

misconceptions.message: B can arrive two ways. Add them: 0.5×0.6 + 0.25×0.4 = 0.4 = 2/5. The A path alone is 0.30 = 3/10.

gold.hint: Exactly one head means head-then-tail or tail-then-head; add both.
gold.display: A biased coin has P(H) = 2/3. It is flipped twice. Find P(exactly one head) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Biased coin: P(H) = 2/3, so P(T) = 1/3. Exactly one head is HT or TH.
P(TH) is the same, 2/9. Two paths, so add the tops.

misconceptions.message: Exactly one head is HT OR TH: 2/9 + 2/9 = 4/9. One order alone is 2/9.

bronze.hint: Count the reds, then divide by the total number of balls.
bronze.display: A bag has 3 red and 5 blue balls. Find P(red) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Probability is favourable outcomes over the total. Start by counting.
So P(red) = favourable over total. Now write the fraction.
guided_steps.hint: The number of reds you counted.

misconceptions.message: Probability is favourable over the TOTAL, not over the rest. There are 3 red out of 8 balls, so P(red) = 3/8. Writing 3/5 compares reds to blues instead.

bronze.hint: Even numbers on a dice are 2, 4 and 6, out of six faces.
bronze.display: A fair dice is rolled. Find P(even number) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: A fair dice has faces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Count the even ones.
So P(even) = 3/6. That simplifies: divide top and bottom by 3.

misconceptions.message: 3 out of 6 is right, but simplify: divide top and bottom by 3 to get 1/2.

bronze.hint: P(not win) = 1 minus P(win); then write the decimal as tenths.
bronze.display: A spinner has P(win) = 0.3. Find P(not win) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: P(not win) means everything except winning: 1 − P(win).

guided_steps.hint: One take away nought point three.

guided_steps.say: Now turn 0.7 into a fraction: 0.7 = 7/10.

misconceptions.message: That is P(win). The question asks P(not win) = 1 − 0.3 = 0.7 = 7/10.

bronze.hint: Favourable over total: mints over all the sweets, then simplify.
bronze.display: There are 15 sweets: 9 toffee and 6 mint. Find P(mint) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Favourable over total. The mints are what we want, then simplify.
So P(mint) = 6/15. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 3.

misconceptions.message: Put mints over the TOTAL of 15 sweets: 6/15 = 2/5. 6/9 compares mints to toffees instead.
6 out of 15 is right, but simplify: divide top and bottom by 3 to get 2/5.

bronze.hint: Add all the counters for the total, then greens over it, and simplify.
bronze.display: A bag has 4 red, 3 green and 5 blue counters. Find P(green) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Total everything first, then put greens over the total and simplify.
So P(green) = 3/12. Simplify by dividing top and bottom by 3.

misconceptions.message: Put greens over the TOTAL of 12: 3/12 = 1/4. 3/9 compares greens to the other colours instead.
3 out of 12 is right, but simplify: divide top and bottom by 3 to get 1/4.

bronze.hint: Expected number = probability × number of trials.
bronze.display: P(rain) = 0.2. The event is repeated 50 times. Find the expected number of rainy days.

guided_steps.say: Expected number = probability × number of trials.

guided_steps.pre: The probability of rain each day =

guided_steps.say: Now multiply them together.

guided_steps.hint: Divide to get back the probability.

misconceptions.message: Expected number = probability × trials = 0.2 × 50 = 10. Dividing 50 by 0.2 gives 250, far too many.

bronze.hint: Count the letter B's, then divide by the total number of letters.
bronze.display: A letter is chosen at random from PROBABILITY. Find P(B) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Spell out PROBABILITY and count the letters.

guided_steps.pre: How many are the letter B?

guided_steps.say: So P(B) = B's over total letters.

misconceptions.message: PROBABILITY has 11 letters and exactly 2 of them are B, so P(B) = 2/11.

bronze.hint: Primes from 1 to 12 are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11. Remember 1 is not prime.
bronze.display: A fair spinner has 12 equal sections numbered 1 to 12. Find P(prime number) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: A prime has exactly two factors. List the primes from 1 to 12.
So P(prime) = primes over total. 5/12 is already simplest.

misconceptions.message: 1 is not prime. The primes from 1 to 12 are 2, 3, 5, 7 and 11: five of them, so 5/12. Counting 1 as prime gives 6/12.

silver.hint: Multiply along the branch: P(H) then P(H) again.
silver.display: A coin is flipped twice. Find P(two heads) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Two flips: draw two branches each time. P(H) = 1/2 every flip.

guided_steps.pre: Two heads needs H then H. Multiply tops: 1 × 1 =
guided_steps.say: Multiply along the H-then-H branch.

misconceptions.message: Two heads needs BOTH flips: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4. 1/2 is the chance of just one head.

silver.hint: With replacement the second pick is identical, so multiply the two equal fractions.
silver.display: A bag has 6 red and 4 blue. Two are picked with replacement. Find P(both blue) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: With replacement the bag is the same each time. P(blue) = 4/10 both picks.
Now simplify 16/100 by dividing by 4.

misconceptions.message: The ball is replaced, so the second pick is still 4/10: 4/10 × 4/10 = 4/25. Dropping the total gives 12/90 = 2/15, the without-replacement answer.

silver.hint: Without replacement the second red is 4/7, not 5/8.
silver.display: A bag has 5 red and 3 blue. Two are picked without replacement. Find P(both red) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Without replacement the second pick has one fewer red and one fewer in total.

guided_steps.pre: After one red is gone, reds left =

guided_steps.say: So P(both red) = 5/8 × 4/7 = 20/56. Simplify by dividing by 4.

misconceptions.message: Without replacement the second red is 4/7, not 5/8: 5/8 × 4/7 = 5/14. Keeping 5/8 twice gives 25/64.

silver.hint: Independent AND means multiply the two probabilities.
silver.display: P(A) = 0.4, P(B) = 0.5. A and B are independent. Find P(A and B) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: Independent AND means multiply the probabilities.
Now 0.2 = 2/10. Simplify by dividing by 2.

misconceptions.message: Independent AND means multiply: 0.4 × 0.5 = 0.2 = 1/5. Adding gives 0.9 = 9/10.

silver.hint: OR with separate colours means add the two probabilities.
silver.display: A bag has 4 red, 3 blue, 3 green. Find P(red or green) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: One pick, two acceptable colours: this is OR, so add the probabilities.
So P(red or green) = 7 over the total.

misconceptions.message: Separate colours on one pick is OR, so add: 4/10 + 3/10 = 7/10. Multiplying gives 12/100 = 3/25.

silver.hint: P(lose) is 2/3 each spin; three losses means cubing it.
silver.display: A spinner has P(win) = 1/3. It is spun 3 times. Find P(no wins) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: No wins in three spins means losing every spin. P(lose) = 1 − 1/3.
Three losses in a row: cube the fraction.

misconceptions.message: Three spins means cubing: (2/3)³ = 8/27. 2/3 is only one spin.

silver.hint: Two orders give one of each: red then blue, and blue then red. Add them.
silver.display: A bag has 8 red and 2 blue. Two picked without replacement. Find P(one red, one blue in any order) as a simplified fraction.

guided_steps.say: One of each can happen two ways: red then blue, or blue then red. Without replacement.

guided_steps.hint: Reds times blues along the path.

guided_steps.say: P(blue-red) works out the same, 16/90. Two paths, so add the tops.

misconceptions.message: One of each happens two ways: red-blue AND blue-red, each 16/90. Add them: 32/90 = 16/45. One order alone is 16/90.

problem_bank.gold_description: Multi-stage and conditional probability: combine several paths, handle picks without replacement, and use the total-probability rule.
problem_bank.bronze_description: Single-event probability: count the favourable outcomes over the total, then write it as a fraction in its simplest form.
problem_bank.silver_description: Two-stage probability: multiply along the branches of a tree for AND, add branches for OR, and drop the second fraction when there is no replacement.
